[spoiler= Part 2 Ragnarök] By the third week of the war, the nation of Chernarus, once stubbornly independent, proud in its neutrality and steeped in post-communist defiance, was now broken and bleeding, brought to its knees under the cold boots of Jomslandic domination.
The initial strike had decapitated Chernaruss command structure within days. The Jomsviking teams, trained in high-speed warfare of all sorts, cut deep into the countryside with machine-like precision, bypassing hardened positions to encircle critical cities, airbases, and uranium deposits. With air superiority firmly established by long-range stealth drones and the legendary JFH-Velum MZKF-23 Sparrowhawk, and cyberwarfare paralyzing internal communication networks, there had never been time for a full national mobilization. What reserves existed were caught in disarray, redeployed to protect already-lost ground.
One by one, the cities folded. One by one, the ministries fell.
Only the capital, Vystok, resisted with any substance. It was here, in the rusting industrial heart of the south, that the last loyalist generals regrouped. In desperation, they fortified entire districts and declared a sacred stand. The citys streets were laced with barricades, burning wreckage, and shattered transport lines. The population had been armed to the teeth. Apartment complexes were turned into sniper nests; metro tunnels into dangerous deathtraps. The industrial sprawl became an improvised fortress.
But even the great bastion of the south could not withstand the fury of the north.
Marshal Hjallmarsson, by then dubbed the Ice Reaver in the Jomslandic press, unleashed Operation Dvergr, a massive, synchronized pincer movement involving underground breach teams, large scale drone attacks, and devastating thermobaric artillery. Street by street, under the cover of ECM fog and persistent psychological operations, the Jomslandic forces reduced the city to a husk.
Dozens of high-value targets were neutralized in coordinated night strikes, guided by biometric tagging and algorithmic heat-mapping. What remained of Chernaruss army detonated their final ammunition stockpiles in a desperate suicide act, collapsing three city blocks and killing hundreds, most of them civilians trapped inside.
Jomsland declared total control over Chernarus by Day 25 of the war.
But for High King Jorik III Blodskald, this conquest was never the end. It was only the beginning.
As the White Dragon banner was raised above the cracked and bullet-ridden senate chamber of Vystok, Jorik summoned the full Althing to Bondahall. From across the fjords and polar provinces, ministers, jarls, scientists, and military lords gathered in the great steel-and-marble dome.
"The conquest is complete, said Jarl Holmgeir of Reikjawik, his tone weary but victorious. The uranium corridors are secure. Wadruna-Prime begins fuel refinement within 72 hours. Weve won, my King.
Jorik stood slowly, his old war wounds stiff beneath the silver-forged armor of the High Kingship.
Victory is not declared by ink, he said. It is burned into memory.
He turned to Lord Akí, Director of the Royal Technological Armory, the man who had quietly revived a ghost from Jomslands Cold Age.
It is time, Jorik said. Unleash Yeldrung.
That same day, across the frozen reaches of Vetrarhald Island, an uninhabited outpost isolated deep in the North Sea, a silence fell unlike any heard in centuries. Beneath ancient glaciers and reinforced basalt, in a facility codenamed Hvítrhǫll, final preparations were underway.
Project Ragnarök II, the rebirth of Jomslands nuclear deterrent, had been accelerated beyond belief. Using classified schematics from the Cold Age, once hidden in the deepest archives of the second Commonwealth, and enriched uranium extracted in the earliest day and weeks of the invasion, the Jomslandic scientists had done the impossible. In under a month, they had built a functioning thermonuclear device from forgotten knowledge and Cold Age Era Parts.
The warhead was named Yeldrung-I, after the legendary weapon of the goddess Wadruna, the mother of Teutons.
The test was scheduled for the 2nd of June, precisely at 23:30 AM.
Across the world, no one suspected anything.
Until the sky broke.
In the darkness before dawn, a fireball brighter than Ardagan itself erupted from beneath the ice. It tore through glaciers like paper and blackened the atmosphere with a towering column of vaporized snow, shattered rock, and irradiated steam. The detonation, clocked at 1.2 megatons, registered across every seismic monitoring station on the northern coast of Jomsland and probably far beyond.
A pulse of radiation carved into the upper atmosphere, temporarily disrupting polar satellite coverage. For brief seconds, an eerie aurora borealis shimmered violently over the horizon, unnatural and red.
The ice of Vetrarhald Island cracked and shifted. Deep fissures ran through its glacial plate. Waves surged in all directions, hammering abandoned weather outposts along the northern Circle.
That same evening, Jorik appeared before the Althing once more, this time in a simple black cloak embroidered with the runes. His voice echoed through the chamber like iron across stone.
Let it be known across the stars and seas: the White Dragon lives.
We rise so that none may strike us down.
We are Jomsland. And we have remembered who we are.
Meanwhile, inside Chernarus, a strange, uneasy quiet settled.
The protectorate status was hastily formalized under the Treaty of Vystok, granting the region nominal autonomy under strict Jomslandic military oversight. Local parliaments were kept in place, but their power was purely ceremonial. Reconstruction of key cities began immediately, focusing on transport infrastructure, mining operations, and re-education centers. Propaganda offices opened in every major city, broadcasting messages of unity, strength, and inevitable victory.
Resistance cells, once active and brave, were now either dismantled or dormant. Most had gone underground, others had fled west. The people had seen the fire on the ice, and knew what came with it.
Wadruna-Prime, the sprawling uranium refinement facility near Lake Ilinalta, expanded rapidly. Dozens of fortified guard towers surrounded it, each armed to the teeth with automated defense drones and surface-to-air machine guns. The uranium veins were tapped with industrial-scale efficiency, feeding not only into Jomslands expanded energy grid but also its newly built nuclear defense complex.
Rumors of a second and third warhead program began to circulate through diplomatic backchannels. Whispers in Elseyran security councils grew louder. Analysts spoke of a "new era." Some called it panic. Others, prophecy.
And as supply ships crossed Lake Ilinalta under heavy naval escort, their grey hulls marked with the sigil of the Jomslandic crown, the message was unmistakable:
The world had changed.
The Age of Fire had begun.[/spoiler] ~1048 words
